import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_27/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_27/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_27/training_2.csv"

# Load Source 0: ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
# index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Load Source 1: ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Load Source 2: ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)

# Transformation plan:
# Target schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float]
# 
# Steps:
# 1. Join df0 and df1 on 'user_id' to get user info (age, occupation) along with ratings.
# 2. Join the result with df2 on 'movie_id' to get the movie title.
# 3. Select and reorder columns to match target schema.
# 4. Convert data types to match target schema:
#    - title: string (already string)
#    - user_id: float (source is int, convert to float)
#    - movie_id: integer (source is int)
#    - rating: float (source is int or float)
#    - timestamp: float (source is int, convert to float)
#    - age: float (source is int, convert to float)
#    - occupation: float (source is int, convert to float)
#
# Note: 'gender' and 'zip' from df1 are not needed in target.
# All source tables are used.
#
# No aggregation or group by needed because user_id and movie_id combinations are unique in df0.
# The target examples show float user_id, so convert user_id to float.
# The timestamp is large integer, convert to float.
# Age and occupation are floats in target, convert accordingly.

# Join df0 and df1 on 'user_id' (inner join to keep only matching users)
df0_1 = pd.merge(df0, df1[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Join the above result with df2 on 'movie_id' (inner join to keep only matching movies)
df_final = pd.merge(df0_1, df2[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Reorder and select columns as per target schema
df_final = df_final[['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']]

# Convert data types
df_final['title'] = df_final['title'].astype(str)
df_final['user_id'] = df_final['user_id'].astype(float)
df_final['movie_id'] = df_final['movie_id'].astype(int)
df_final['rating'] = df_final['rating'].astype(float)
df_final['timestamp'] = df_final['timestamp'].astype(float)
df_final['age'] = df_final['age'].astype(float)
df_final['occupation'] = df_final['occupation'].astype(float)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_27/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_27/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_27/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_27/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source0 and Source1 on user_id
join_0_1 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source2 on movie_id
joined = pd.merge(join_0_1, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Reorder columns to match target schema before aggregation
# Target schema: ['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']
joined = joined[['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']]

# Group by leftmost non-float columns that are unique identifiers in target examples:
# title (string), user_id (float but used as group key), movie_id (integer)
# Aggregate other columns by mean as target examples show averages
result = joined.groupby(['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id'], as_index=False).agg({
    'rating': 'mean',
    'timestamp': 'mean',
    'age': 'mean',
    'occupation': 'mean'
})

# Write output to the specified file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_27/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
